newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast parliament speaker Donwahi dies.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast parliament speaker Donwahi dies.

text.p: Ivory Coast's parliamentary speaker Charles Bauza Donwahi, the constitutional successor to the head of state, died on Saturday at his home after a battle with cancer, family sources said.
Donwahi, who was 71, had been admitted to a Paris hospital for prostate cancer treatment but was brought back home about two weeks ago as his condition deteriorated, the sources said.

He was elected speaker of the National Assembly after Henri Konan Bedie vacated the post to succeed veteran president Felix Houphouet-Boigny, who died on December 7, 1993. Donwahi was re-elected in December 1995 for a five-year term.
Under Ivory Coast's constitution, the assembly speaker succeeds the president for an interim period in the event of death or incapacity to perform his officail functions.
